authorityCeiling.basis: MOTHER / governance performs the Section 3.4 intersection: the executable topology is the intersection of proposed, allowed, and available capability. Only governance can reduce or block a proposed topology, and Section 3.3 lists emergency block as the top authority level, so its ceiling is emergency-block.

Section 3.4: "The executable topology is the intersection of what the planner proposes, what policy permits, and what infrastructure can currently provide." Section 3.3 authority vocabulary includes emergency block, the level that enforces that intersection.

capabilityFamilies.basis: Role quote: "Intersects proposed topology with allowed and available capability." Section 3.4: "Each reduction should produce a machine-readable governance receipt." Boundary quote: "Health monitoring and epistemic/policy governance remain distinct contracts."

lifecycleStages.basis: Section 3.3 defines lifecycleMask as workflow stage and completion state but names no stages. The paper assigns no lifecycle stages to MOTHER / governance.

memoryPlanes.basis: The paper assigns no memory planes to MOTHER / governance. Governance intersects proposed, allowed, and available capability; no memory plane is named for that function.

outputClasses.basis: Section 3.4: "Each reduction should produce a machine-readable governance receipt." A governance receipt is a recorded artifact.

permittedRoutes.basis: The paper defines routeMask semantics in Sections 3.2 and 3.3 but names no per-organ routes for MOTHER / governance.

paperBoundary: Health monitoring and epistemic/policy governance remain distinct contracts.
paperRole: Intersects proposed topology with allowed and available capability.
paperSource: N-Cell position paper, Section 4 mapping table, https://ncell-position-paper.pages.dev/, accessed 2026-11-14.
